title: Analysis of biomarkers in the peripheral blood of patients with soft tissue sarcoma
summary:
Sarcomas are malignant tumors of connective tissue origin with high disease-related mortality (5-year survival approx. 50%). The tumor stage, which is mainly determined by the time of diagnosis, is crucial for the prognosis. Treatment is interdisciplinary and consists, depending on the subtype, of surgical resection, radiation and chemotherapy. Diagnosis and follow-up are currently only possible by taking the patient's medical history and clinical examination, imaging procedures and tumor biopsy with histopathological work-up. Due to their rarity, knowledge about these diseases is very limited and specific diagnostic and therapeutic options are limited.
In order to develop new diagnostic tests, the DNA of the tumor and free circulating DNA in the blood is examined for tumor-specific genetic changes. On the other hand, the presence of the SYT-SSX fusion gene transcript in microvesicles delivered by synovial sarcoma cells and its role as a biomarker for synovial sarcoma will be investigated. In addition, miRNA profiles of patients with synovial sarcoma will be generated in order to differentiate tumor patients from healthy individuals using a blood sample to improve tumor aftercare.
The required blood samples are taken during tumor treatment and aftercare and stored in a special sarcoma biobank. Blood withdrawals are carried out at the time of the regular follow-up examinations. In addition, tumor tissue, which is generated during surgery and is not needed for further diagnosis and therapy, is stored.
Subsequently, tumor-specific changes in the tissue and blood are detected with modern analytical methods to determine the activity of the tumor disease in the blood. In the future, this will allow non-invasive monitoring of both therapy response and follow-up examinations.
